items.headline: 【ウェビナー】日銀9月会合直前 ― 利上げ「過去最速」のペースとなるか
items.summary: 日本銀行の利上げペースと、金融市場を取り巻く構造はどう変化するのか。 ブルームバーグニュースによる本ウェビナーでは、元日銀で政策決定会合向けの分析に携わってきたシニアエコノミストの木村太郎と、海外投資家や市場の動向を追うマーケット担当記者のアリス・フレンチが登壇。リニューアルした日本語版ニュースサイトのマネジングエディター野上英文がMCを務め、ニュースの行間を読み解く視点を探ります。 (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: UK to Gain From Replacing Oil Windfall Tax Early, Lobby Says
items.summary: The UK could raise an additional £15 billion ($20 billion) in tax revenue from oil and gas production over the next decade if Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s government brought forward its new fiscal regime to next year, according to an industry lobby group.
items.author: Olga Tanas

items.headline: BOE May End Long-Dated Bond Sales as Officials Draft Plans, Report Says
items.summary: The Bank of England could soon stop selling long-dated bonds that it amassed after the financial crisis and pandemic, according to a report by the Daily Telegraph, in a move that would be likely to save the Treasury billions of pounds.
items.author: Tom Rees, Philip Aldrick and James Hirai

items.headline: India’s Trade Gap Narrows Unexpectedly After Exports Surge
items.summary: India’s trade deficit in August narrowed more than any economist expected on robust export growth, though instability across the Middle East continues to pose a risk to supply chains.
items.author: Shruti Srivastava

items.headline: Sri Lanka’s Growth Misses Forecast as Middle East Crisis Bites
items.summary: Sri Lanka’s economy grew slower than expected last quarter, with elevated oil prices from renewed hostilities in the US-Iran war clouding the outlook for the island nation’s recovery.
items.author: Anusha Ondaatjie

items.headline: UK State Pension Becomes Liable for Tax For the First Time
items.summary: Britain’s state pension is set to rise above £13,000 ($17,516) a year after official wage data indicated the increase next April will be 3.9%.
items.author: Philip Aldrick

items.headline: Bessent’s Growth Solution for US Debt Is Seen Failing the Credibility Test
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has insisted faster economic growth can wipe away concerns about troubling fiscal trajectories, a key theme of his recent G20 leadership. History suggests otherwise.
items.author: Yash Roy

items.headline: French Finance Chiefs Say Debt Issuance Assured as Yields Rise
items.summary: France’s central bank chief and finance minister said the banking sector is resilient and that the country’s debt issuance is assured as global bond yields spike.
items.author: William Horobin

items.headline: Unusual Calm in UK Pound Is Red Flag to Traders Before Budget
items.summary: A measure of UK pound volatility is flashing warning signs that markets are too complacent in the run-up to Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s first Budget.
items.author: Vassilis Karamanis and Alice Gledhill

items.headline: China Stuck in Economic Slow Lane Relies on AI-Fueled Export Boom
items.summary: China’s domestic economy remains stuck in the slow lane, with the AI boom keeping exports afloat.
items.author: Malcolm Scott

items.headline: WTO and rules of global trade
items.summary: Three-quarters of trade still moves on WTO terms, but many rules are slowly being eroded
items.author: Brendan Murray

items.headline: Mexico Tourism Hit by Falling Beach Visits from Big Spending Foreigners
items.summary: Mexico is trying to figure out how to reignite growth at its once-booming beach destinations, where visits by big-spending travelers have slowed in another bleak sign for a struggling economy.
items.author: Gonzalo Soto

items.headline: Switzerland Needs Reforms to Keep Its Global Lead, OECD Says
items.summary: Switzerland must embrace tax and pension reforms to preserve its status as one of the world’s top economies, the OECD said, raising its growth forecast for the country.
items.author: Bastian Benrath-Wright

items.headline: Nigerian Inflation Unexpectedly Eases, Boosts Rate-Cut Case
items.summary: Nigeria’s annual inflation rate unexpectedly fell in August, improving the case for policymakers to resume their easing cycle next week.
items.author: Nduka Orjinmo

items.headline: Angola Bucks Global Trend And Cuts Key Rate as Iran War Rages
items.summary: Angola’s central bank extended its easing cycle as inflation continued to cool, bucking a global trend of policymakers raising or holding rates as the Iran war rages on.
items.author: Candido Mendes

items.headline: Rep. Waters Presses Bessent on Inflation, Iran and Tariffs
items.summary: US Representative Maxine Waters (D-CA) sharply criticizes US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent during his House Finance panel testimony, blaming the administration’s tariffs, trade fights and Iran policy for higher prices and rising borrowing costs. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Peru’s Economy Rebounded in July to Top Forecasts
items.summary: Peru’s economy rebounded in July, driven by strong results across most sectors, even as unusually warmer weather weighed on fishing, agriculture and related industries.
items.author: Carla Samon Ros

items.headline: UK Budget to Be Based on a Single Set of Economic Forecasts
items.summary: Britain’s fiscal watchdog will produce just one economic forecast before the Treasury decides on its budget policies in a bid to make the process more predictable and give the Chancellor of the Exchequer longer to prepare, according to a person familiar.
items.author: Philip Aldrick

items.headline: History Shows Fed Will Deliver Rate Hike Markets Have Locked In
items.summary: Bond traders are pricing in a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike Wednesday with a level of conviction that has proven right for decades.
items.author: Ye Xie and Anya Andrianova

items.headline: Bessent Says US Yen Intervention Was ‘Nominal,’ Backs US Exports
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US only deployed a “nominal” amount in its coordinated intervention to prop up Japan’s currency, and defended that operation as in American interests.
items.author: Yash Roy

people.name: Tom Rees, Philip Aldrick and James Hirai
